title: Practice 5: Rain falls, time flies, luck comes: the idioms

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: А ___ (везти — to convey by vehicle, one way) бы воз, никакой бы муки не видала.
exercises.why: **везла** is the past tense (feminine) of **везти** (to convey, to carry (by vehicle), to deliver, to transport) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **возить** for many directions. past: он вёз · она везла́ · оно везло́ · они везли́. — Wiktionary, «везти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **везти**: to convey, to carry (by vehicle), to deliver, to transport; (impersonal) to be lucky, to have luck, to work out for, to succeed, to be successful [with dative ‘for someone’ and infinitive ‘to do something’].  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «везти — Ей везёт / повезло. — She is lucky/got lucky.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note also the following idiomatic construction: Мне не везёт. — I am not lucky. Ему везёт. — He is lucky. Вам повезло. — You were lucky.» — DLI, Lesson 78.  ·  From Лев Толстой, «Вторая русская книга для чтения».
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Она ___ (вести — to lead, take along, one way) себя со мной очень конспиративно.
exercises.why: **вела** is the past tense (feminine) of **вести** (to lead, to preside over, to chair) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **водить** for many directions. past: он вёл · она вела́ · оно вело́ · они вели́. — Wiktionary, «вести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **вести**: to lead, to preside over, to chair; to drive; to keep.  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «вести — Страна ведёт войну. — The country is waging a war. · Девочка ведёт дневник. — The girl keeps a diary. · Дорога ведёт в город. — The road leads to the city. · Ложь к добру не ведёт. — No good comes from lying.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «This verb also follows the pattern of "going verbs". Note the following meanings: 1. to lead, to take: Я веду моего сына в школу. Я каждый день вожу его в школу. 2. to drive: Кто ведёт эту машину? Он не умеет водить машину. 3. to conduct: Противник ведёт огонь. 4. to behave oneself: Этот мальчик плохо ведёт себя. Note that in the last two examples (3 and 4) only the actual function verb "вести" can be used. (Never "водить").» — DLI, Lesson 78.  ·  From Максим Горький, «Жизнь Клима Самгина».
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Почему мне ___ (лезть — to climb, one way) в голову именно такие мысли, не понимаю!
exercises.why: **лезли** is the past tense (plural) of **лезть** (to climb (up, on to), to scramble) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **лазить** for many directions. past: он ле́з · она ле́зла · оно ле́зло · они ле́зли. — Wiktionary, «лезть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **лезть**: to climb (up, on to), to scramble; to clamber, to crawl, to scramble (through, into, under); to get (into); to thrust the hand (into).  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «лезть — Хулиганы лезут в драку. — The hooligans are getting into a brawl.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  From Антон Чехов, «Тапёр».
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Не надо думать о таких пустяках — чего они ___ (лезть — to climb, one way) в голову!
exercises.why: **лезут** is the present tense (3rd person plural) of **лезть** (to climb (up, on to), to scramble) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **лазить** for many directions. present: я ле́зу · ты ле́зешь · он ле́зет · мы ле́зем · вы ле́зете · они ле́зут. — Wiktionary, «лезть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **лезть**: to climb (up, on to), to scramble; to clamber, to crawl, to scramble (through, into, under); to get (into); to thrust the hand (into).  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Я люблю людей, о которых ___ (ходить — to go, walk, there and back or in general) слухи.
exercises.why: **ходят** is the present tense (3rd person plural) of **ходить** (to go, to walk) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **идти** for one direction. present: я хожу́ · ты хо́дишь · он хо́дит · мы хо́дим · вы хо́дите · они хо́дят. — Wiktionary, «ходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **ходить**: to go, to walk; to wear something (imperfective only); to go (to), to attend, to visit; to run (of trains, ships, etc.).  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «ходить — Ходит слух, что она бросила мужа. — Rumor has it that she left her husband.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note the following expressions: Идёт дождь. Фильм идёт. Разговор идёт. Идёт снег. Урок идёт. Работа идёт. Поезд идёт. Дорога идёт. Собрание идёт.» — DLI, Lesson 19.  ·  From Юрий Тынянов, «Кюхля».
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: ___ (носить — to carry on foot, there and back or in general) очки, чтоб ничего не видеть.
exercises.why: **носите** is the present tense (2nd person plural) of **носить** (to carry, to bear (a burden)) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **нести** for one direction. present: я ношу́ · ты но́сишь · он но́сит · мы но́сим · вы но́сите · они но́сят. — Wiktionary, «носить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **носить**: to carry, to bear (a burden); (of wind, water, etc.) to carry along, to drive; to have something (e.g. a name, sideburns, a gun...); to wear (clothes, shoes or makeup).  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «носить — Иван Иванович носит имя отца. — Ivan Ivanovich bears the name of his father. · Она носит красивую одежду. — She wears pretty clothing.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note some special uses of these verbs: нести ответственность — to bear responsibility; нести потери — to suffer casualties; носить костюм (пальто, шляпу, ботинки etc.) — to wear (habitually); носить очки — to wear glasses.» — DLI, Lesson 78.  ·  From Максим Горький, «Жизнь Клима Самгина».
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Поезд ___ (идти — to go, walk, one way) мимо диких, угрюмых гор, пробираясь вдоль русла реки.
exercises.why: **шёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **идти** (to go) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **ходить** for many directions. past: он шёл · она шла́ · оно шло́ · они шли́. — Wiktionary, «идти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **идти**: to go; to walk; (of precipitation) to fall; to function, to work (of clocks and watches).  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «идти — Идёт не дождь, а снег. — It's snowing, not raining. · Часы идут. — The clock is ticking. · Идёт фильм. — A film is on. · Это платье тебе идёт. — That dress suits you. · Правительство идёт к демократии. — The government is moving towards democracy.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note the following expressions: Идёт дождь. exercises.q: Роллинг пришел в ярость, — его ___ (водить — to lead, take along, there and back or in general) за нос.
exercises.why: **водили** is the past tense (plural) of **водить** (to lead, to conduct, to guide) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **вести** for one direction. past: он води́л · она води́ла · оно води́ло · они води́ли. — Wiktionary, «водить» (CC BY-SA 4.0). Note that in the last two examples (3 and 4) only the actual function verb "вести" can be used. (Never "водить").» — DLI, Lesson 78.  ·  From Алексей Н. Толстой, «Гиперболоид инженера Гарина».

exercises.q: В один день можно было много сработать, и притом время ___ (бежать — to run, one way) быстро, незаметно.
exercises.why: **бежало** is the past tense (neuter) of **бежать** ((imperfective only) to run, to be running) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **бегать** for many directions. past: он бежа́л · она бежа́ла · оно бежа́ло · они бежа́ли. — Wiktionary, «бежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **бежать**: (imperfective only) to run, to be running; to flee, to be fleeing; to avoid, to be avoiding, to shun, to be shunning; to run after [with за (za, + instrumental) ‘someone’].  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «бежать — Кровь бежит из раны. — Blood is flowing from the wound. · Дни бегут. — The days fly past.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  From Антон Чехов, «Моя жизнь».
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: И этот дурацкий цветок… когда висели драпри, он не ___ (лезть — to climb, one way) в глаза так… нахально!
exercises.why: **лез** is the past tense (masculine) of **лезть** (to climb (up, on to), to scramble) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **лазить** for many directions. past: он ле́з · она ле́зла · оно ле́зло · они ле́зли. — Wiktionary, «лезть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **лезть**: to climb (up, on to), to scramble; to clamber, to crawl, to scramble (through, into, under); to get (into); to thrust the hand (into).  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «лезть — Хулиганы лезут в драку. — The hooligans are getting into a brawl.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  From Максим Горький, «Последний день».
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Якову казалось, что Тихон говорит и ___ (вести — to lead, take along, one way) себя более «по-хозяйски», чем отец.
exercises.why: **ведёт** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **вести** (to lead, to preside over, to chair) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **водить** for many directions. present: я веду́ · ты ведёшь · он ведёт · мы ведём · вы ведёте · они веду́т. — Wiktionary, «вести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **вести**: to lead, to preside over, to chair; to drive; to keep.  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «вести — Страна ведёт войну. — The country is waging a war. · Девочка ведёт дневник. — The girl keeps a diary. · Дорога ведёт в город. — The road leads to the city. · Ложь к добру не ведёт. — No good comes from lying.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «This verb also follows the pattern of "going verbs". Note the following meanings: 1. to lead, to take: Я веду моего сына в школу. Я каждый день вожу его в школу. 2. to drive: Кто ведёт эту машину? Он не умеет водить машину. 3. to conduct: Противник ведёт огонь. 4. to behave oneself: Этот мальчик плохо ведёт себя. Note that in the last two examples (3 and 4) only the actual function verb "вести" can be used. (Never "водить").» — DLI, Lesson 78.  ·  From Максим Горький, «Дело Артамоновых».
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Зато уж не прогневайтесь: она у меня ___ (носить — to carry on foot, there and back or in general) имя, как человек.
exercises.why: **носит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **носить** (to carry, to bear (a burden)) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **нести** for one direction. present: я ношу́ · ты но́сишь · он но́сит · мы но́сим · вы но́сите · они но́сят. — Wiktionary, «носить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **носить**: to carry, to bear (a burden); (of wind, water, etc.) to carry along, to drive; to have something (e.g. a name, sideburns, a gun...); to wear (clothes, shoes or makeup).  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «носить — Иван Иванович носит имя отца. — Ivan Ivanovich bears the name of his father. · Она носит красивую одежду. — She wears pretty clothing.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note some special uses of these verbs: нести ответственность — to bear responsibility; нести потери — to suffer casualties; носить костюм (пальто, шляпу, ботинки etc.) — to wear (habitually); носить очки — to wear glasses.» — DLI, Lesson 78.  ·  From Николай Гоголь, «Игроки».
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))
